BY ADV V.A.OMANAKUTTAN RESPONDENT/2ND RESPONDENT:
 THE RELIANCE GENERAL INSURANCE  KOCHI-31.
 BY ADV TAPAS VARMA .

A  THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 07.04.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 2025:KER:30025 MACA NO.3322 OF 2017  3
JUDGMENT

The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No.1272/2014 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Ernakulam, is the appellant herein.
During the pendency of the appeal the original appellant died and his legal heirs were impleaded as additional appellants 2 to 5.
Thereafter, additional 4 th appellant also died and his legal heirs were impleaded as additional appellants 6 to 8.

(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2.
The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 03.05.2014.

According to the petitioner, on 03.05.2014 at about 6 a.m., while he was standing by the side of Kakkanadu-Palarivattom road, a motorcycle bearing reg.no.KL 45 K 3380 ridden by the 1st respondent in a rash and negligent manner knocked down the petitioner and as a result of the accident, the petitioner sustained serious injuries.

sentences.text: The 1st respondent is the rider cum owner and the 2nd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioner, the 2025:KER:30025 MACA NO.3322 OF 2017 accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. is Rs.34,00,000/- limited to Rs.20,00,000/-.
4. The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
5. The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimony of PW1 and documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A19 and X1.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.

6. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.13,25,450/- and directed the insurer to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?

9. Heard Sri.V.A.Omanakuttan, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner/appellant, and Sri.Tapas Varma A, the learned Standing 2025:KER:30025 MACA NO.3322 OF 2017 Counsel for the 2nd respondent.
10. The Point:
In this case the accident as well as valid insurance policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is regarding the income of the petitioner as fixed by the Tribunal.
According to him, the petitioner was engaged in real estate business, earning Rs.10,000/- per month, but the Tribunal fixed his monthly income at Rs.5000/-.
The learned counsel for the insurer would argue that the income fixed by the tribunal is reasonable.

11. As per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie, in the year 2014 will come to Rs.9500/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Since the petitioner could not prove his job or income as claimed in the OP, in the light of a dictum laid down in the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa (supra) , his notional income is liable to be fixed as that of a coolie, at Rs.9500/-.
12.

In the accident the petitioner sustained the following injuries:

3  Fracture to the neck of right femur, fracture shaft of right femur, fracture to the neck of right fibula, 2025:KER:30025 MACA NO.3322 OF 2017 fracture proximal tibia right and fracture of scapula right.

sentences.text: 13. Ext.X1 disability certificate shows that the petitioner suffered 23% permanent physical disability.
It was issued by the medical board.
The Tribunal, however, considering the gravity of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, fixed his functional disability at 40% and it is not under challenge.

14. Since, on the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 74 years, there is no scope for any future prospects and the multiplier to be applied is 5, as held in Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation, [(2009) 6 SCC 121].

entities.text: Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation, [(2009) 6 SCC 121]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the above circumstances, the loss of disability will come to Rs.2,28,000/-.
15. Towards loss of earning, the tribunal has awarded Rs.120000/- being the income for 24 months @ Rs.5000/-.

Since the notional income of the petitioner is re-fixed at Rs.9500/-, towards loss of earning he is entitled to get a sum of Rs.2,28,000/-(9500 x 24 months)
16.
Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.85000/-.
Towards 'loss of amenities of life' Rs.40000/- was awarded.
According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, the 2025:KER:30025 MACA NO.3322 OF 2017 compensation awarded on those heads are on the lower side.
17. The petitioner sustained very serious injuries in the accident and was treated as inpatient for 166 days in 5 spells.
In the meantime he had undergone 7 surgeries also.

Because of the injuries sustained, the percentage of disability suffered and the length of treatment undergone by the petitioner, I hold that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the heads 'pain and sufferings'
and 'loss of amenities of life' are on the lower side and hence they are enhanced to Rs.1,00,000/-,
and Rs.75,000/- respectively.
18.
No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.

19. Therefore, the petitioners/appellants are entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.16,39,450/-,
as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference:
Sl.
 No. Head of Claim Amount awarded by Amount Awarded in  Tribunal (in Rs.) Appeal (in Rs.)
1 Loss of earning 120000 228000
2 Transport to hospital and back to 25000 25000  home  3 Extra nourishment 18000 18000
4 Damage to clothing and articles 5000 5000

In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit a total sum of Rs.16,39,450/- (Rupees Sixteen Lakhs Thirty Nine Thousand Four Hundred and Fifty only), less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest at the rate ordered by the Tribunal, from the date of the petition till deposit/realisation, with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.
(Enhanced compensation will carry interest @8%)
On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the entire amount to the petitioner, excluding court fee payable, if any, without delay, as per rules.
